plan.notes: SOURCE: https://engineering.tufts.edu/cs/current-students/policies-and-documentation — Department of Computer Science, Tufts University School of Engineering, 'Bachelor of Science in Computer Science - School of Engineering' section (retrieved 2026-09-30). This plan transcribes the department's official SAMPLE PROGRAM verbatim, term by term (First Year Fall through Senior Year Spring), as published: 'The following sample program is one way of satisfying the above requirements.' Term sequences were cross-checked against the BSCS requirements text on the same page (introductory / HASS / breadth / engineering / CS-major requirements). CATALOG-YEAR CAVEAT: Tufts publishes this BSCS sample program WITHOUT a class year (it is year-agnostic); catalog_year is recorded as '2026-2027', the year of transcription (2026-09-30). Confirm currency with the department before use. CREDIT TOTAL: the sample program as transcribed sums to 115 semester-hour units (SHU) — 5 SHU BELOW the degree's stated 120-SHU minimum ('The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BSCS) requires a minimum of 120 semester-hours of study'). Per-course SHU basis, all from official Tufts sources: 3 SHU is the Tufts standard ('a class worth three semester-hours — the majority of classes at Tufts'); 4 SHU for laboratory/project courses — Physics 11, Chemistry 1/16, Biology 13 (all listed 'w/Lab'), Computer Science 11 (weekly lab), 15, 40, 105, 160 (Data Structures = 4 cr and Algorithms = 4 cr per the official Tufts School of Engineering online post-bacc course list); 3 SHU for Computer Science 61 (Discrete Mathematics = 3 cr), 97/98 (Senior Capstone), 170 (Theory of Computation = 3 cr, same official list), all Mathematics, all Engineering (EN 1, ES 2/3/4, ES 56, EN 54), English 1, each HASS elective (24-SHU HASS requirement / 8 courses = 3 SHU each), the breadth elective (6-SHU breadth / EN 54 + 1 elective), each CS concentration elective (3-SHU standard per the requirements text), and the natural-science/mathematics elective (requirements text says '3 or more' SHU; transcribed at the 3-SHU minimum). Students following this sample would need higher-SHU elective choices (e.g., a 4-SHU lab science or CS elective) or additional coursework to reach the 120-SHU minimum. BOX DEGREE SHEETS NOT USED: the tufts.box.com degree-sheet links were excluded as unverifiable per source policy; students.tufts.edu links only to those Box shares and was likewise not used. PREREQUISITES reflect the sample program's own term sequencing (e.g., Mathematics 34 after 32; Computer Science 15 after 11 — the latter stated explicitly as 'Prerequisite: COMP 11' on cs.tufts.edu); where a prerequisite is satisfied by a student-choice slot, the prereq points at the choice slot's own code (e.g., COMP 160 lists the Discrete Mathematics choice slot). No courses, credits, or prerequisites were invented; every student-choice slot uses choice:true with a placeholder code. Credential: BS in Computer Science, School of Engineering, Tufts University (Medford, MA).
